summary: Round-8 verify, run alone on a quiescent tree. METHOD, so the numbers can be re-derived: unmutated baseline `./gradlew :sequencer:test --tests 'binjava.sequencer.FaultInjectingStore*'` = 19 tests / 0 failures (14 in FaultInjectingStoreTest, 5 in FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest). Each mutant applied to sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/FaultInjectingStore.java only, sequencer/build/test-results/test deleted before each run, the killing test read out of the JUnit XML rather than from the console, and every mutant reverted with `git checkout --`. Tree left exactly as found: three staged adds, one staged modify, the five M4.19/M4.20 files still untracked, and `git diff --cached | sha256sum` still 404e39d8679f. CLOSED, each by measurement. Y1 (stale count): the M4.12 row carries no number, names both test classes, and describes coverage instead. Y2/Y3 (the counting test could not see draw-vs-branch order or read-verb wiring): moving putIfMatch's two alignment draws BELOW the ambiguous branch now fails everyClassDrawsOnEVERYFaultingCall... on the new firing phase; re-pointing stat to ambiguousDraws, get to duplicateDraws and list to duplicateDraws each fail its quiet phase on the 7/4/4 map. The map is arithmetically right and its as() message matches the calls -- three putIfAbsent plus one putIfMatch is four conditional writes drawing all three streams, plus stat/get/list drawing unreachable only, so 7/4/4 -- and it is not brittle: it is a closed count over the seven calls written three lines above it, not a property of a seed. Y4/Y5/Y6: @Timeout is on both classes, no unused imports, no orphaned javadoc. W1/W2 from the test reviewer: degrading putIfAbsent's landing write to `delegate.put` now fails anAmbiguousPutIfAbsentSTILLLOSESToAnOccupiedSlot..., and degrading putIfMatch's to a version-less `delegate.put` now fails anAmbiguousPutIfMatchSTILLLOSESToASTALEVersion.... The zeroed same-length payload dies on both ambiguous arms (putIfAbsent by the new test at :369, putIfMatch by the existing test at :143). The countDraw javadoc's claim is CORRECT and I measured both halves: swapping the ambiguousPut/duplicatePut labels survives all 19 tests, swapping unreachable/ambiguousPut fails the count map -- so the stated reason (both streams drawn exactly once per conditional write, never by a read verb, hence equal in every workload) holds for the current verb set. NOT CLOSED, and this is the round's finding: the round-7 fixes closed three doors on the FAULTING arms and left the identical two open on the CLEAN arms, which is the path every non-faulted call in M4.13's sweep takes. Writing a same-length zeroed payload on putIfAbsent's clean landing write survives all 19 tests, and returning `Optional.of(delegate.put(k, b))` from putIfMatch's clean path -- the version dropped, verbatim the mutant this commit's own new test comment calls 'the zombie write M4.16 spent three rounds diagnosing as an I2 violation' -- also survives all 19. Both filed as major. Four minors on prose and two uncovered pass-throughs. No object-store request-rate concern: the decorator is test-only, adds no request that scales with records, shards, partitions or indices, and the one extra conditional write it does add is the duplicatePut fault itself, per call and bounded by its probability.

findings.finding: SURVIVING MUTATION, MEASURED: the payload written on the NON-FAULTING putIfAbsent path is unconstrained. I replaced `new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes)` at line 216 with `new ByteArrayInputStream(new byte[bytes.length])` -- the right length, all zeroes -- and all 19 tests passed (gradle exit 0). This is verbatim the defect the new test at FaultInjectingStoreTest.java:369 was written to close, one branch over: that test drives Faults(0, 1.0, 0) so it only ever reaches the AMBIGUOUS arm, and no test in either class reads back a payload that went through the clean arm. aStoreConfiguredWithNoFaults... writes 200 objects and reads none; aDUPLICATEDPut... counts puts through CountingBinStore and checks the Optional, not the bytes; the streams tests write 60-120 objects each and never read; the one `quiet.get("a")` in the count test closes the stream without asserting its content. The clean arm is the one every non-faulted call in M4.13's 1,000-seed sweep takes, so it carries essentially all of the sweep's data. Note this also leaves W3 ('the hand-rolled copy at three sites') only partly closed: of the four copy sites, the two ambiguous arms are now pinned, the duplicate retry is an equivalent mutant (the retry can never land against a write-once primitive -- I measured it surviving, correctly), and this one is a live hole.
findings.failure_scenario: A later hand tidies the buffer-and-rewrap dance -- hoisting the three `new Body(bytes.length, () -> new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes))` constructions into a helper, or reusing a single ByteArrayInputStream that a second call finds already drained -- and the clean path starts writing empty or truncated bodies. Every test stays green. M4.13 then runs 1,000 seeds, the chain entries fail to decode, and the sweep reports a corrupt commit log for seeds the protocol wrote perfectly. The row for M4.13 says its whole purpose is that 'every failing seed is pinned as a named regression test'; those regressions would be pinned against the harness. The fix is one line: assert the round-tripped bytes after a clean putIfAbsent through the injector, exactly as :369 does after a faulted one.

findings.line: 277 (`return delegate.putIfMatch(k, b, v);`, putIfMatch's clean path)
findings.finding: SURVIVING MUTATION, MEASURED: the clean putIfMatch path can drop the version. I replaced line 277 with `return Optional.of(delegate.put(k, b));` and all 19 tests passed (gradle exit 0). The new test anAmbiguousPutIfMatchSTILLLOSESToASTALEVersionAndLandsNothing (:389) closes exactly this mutant on the AMBIGUOUS arm and its own comment says why it matters -- 'that mutant IS the zombie write M4.16 spent three rounds diagnosing as an I2 violation, manufactured by the harness rather than by the protocol' -- but it runs at Faults(0, 1.0, 0), so it never reaches line 277. Nothing else does either: the only clean putIfMatch in the suite is `quiet.putIfMatch("c", body("v2"), version.orElseThrow())` at FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest.java:231, which is there to bump a draw count and asserts nothing about its result or about the store. So the argument the author made for the ambiguous arm applies unchanged to the clean arm and was not carried across -- and the clean arm is where every lease CAS in the simulation actually goes, since ambiguousPut is a low-probability fault.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.13's sweep drives many logical pods through LeaseManager, whose only CAS is putIfMatch. With the version dropped on the clean path every lease CAS succeeds unconditionally, so fencing never works: a pod that lost the lease keeps renewing it, two leaders believe they hold the same slot, and the sweep reports I2 violations across a wide band of seeds. M4.16 already documents three rounds spent chasing seeds for exactly this symptom -- 'the seeds have moved twice' -- and the next occurrence would be attributed to LocalSequencer.start's ancestor sealing again, because the row says that is the known cause. The harness must be the one thing in the sweep that cannot be the suspect. Fix: give the clean path the same stale-version test the ambiguous path just got -- seed a version, move the object on, call putIfMatch through a Faults.none() injector with the stale version, and assert an empty Optional and an unchanged object.

findings.finding: THE NAME PROMISES A PROPERTY THE TEST CANNOT HAVE. `anAmbiguousPutIfAbsentSTILLLOSESToAnOccupiedSlotAndCarriesTHECALLERSBytes` asserts one thing: that the slot owner's bytes ('A-was-here') survive. It never looks at the caller's bytes -- and on this path it cannot, because the conditional write LOSES, so 'B-loses' never lands anywhere. The 'carries the caller's bytes' half is a different test's job (:369, on a free key). A test name is the only summary a later reader gets, and this one asserts coverage of a property that is not merely unasserted here but unobservable here. This file's own history is a chain of exactly this defect at one level up ('the row described a commit other than itself'), which is why it is worth the line.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone auditing which properties of the ambiguous arm are pinned reads the two test names, sees 'STILL LOSES ... AND CARRIES THE CALLER'S BYTES' and 'WRITES THE CALLER'S EXACT BYTES', concludes the second is redundant with the first, and deletes it -- restoring the zeroed-payload hole round 7 measured, with the suite green and a name still claiming the property. Rename to `...STILLLOSESToAnOccupiedSlotRatherThanCLOBBERINGIt`.

findings.finding: THE COMMENT NAMES A MUTATION THE TEST DOES NOT KILL, and I measured both gaps. The comment says 'Surviving mutations included swapping getRange's bounds, making delete a no-op, and making close a no-op' -- and the test then exercises put, getRange and delete, but never calls `close()` or `multipart()`. Measured: making `close()` a no-op survives all 19 tests (gradle exit 0), and re-keying `multipart(k)` to `multipart(k + "-wrong")` survives all 19 tests (gradle exit 0). The backlog row's coverage sentence inherits the over-claim: 'faithful delegation of the verbs that inject nothing' covers two of the four verbs it names plus close.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.20's driver, or M4.9's request-count assertions, wrap a store whose close() releases something real (a MinIO client, a temp directory, an executor) and the injector silently swallows it, or a later multipart path writes to the wrong key. The comment tells the next reader those verbs are pinned, so nobody re-measures. Two more lines in the same test -- `store.close()` against a delegate that records it, and one multipart write read back under its own key -- close both, or the comment should say which verbs it does not reach.

findings.line: 159-166 (the 'AND IT IS FIXABLE' paragraph on countDraw)
findings.finding: THE FIXABILITY CLAIM OVERSTATES ITS RUNG. The first half of the paragraph is right and I measured it: the ambiguousPut/duplicatePut label swap survives all 19 tests while the unreachable/ambiguousPut swap dies, exactly as the note says, and the stated reason (both drawn once per conditional write, neither drawn by a read verb, so equal in every workload) is sound for the current verb set. But 'a stream that carries its own name would make the mutation unrepresentable rather than merely untested -- rung 1 instead of rung 6' is not true of the design it describes. A self-naming stream still has a construction site where the name and the scramble index are paired by hand -- `new NamedStream("ambiguousPut", scramble(seed, 2))` -- and swapping the two literals there is the same mislabelling arriving one step earlier. What self-naming buys is that the label stops being RE-DERIVED by reference comparison at every draw: one site instead of a guess, which is gate-design rung 2 (derive it from a source of truth), not rung 1 (make the bad state unrepresentable).
findings.failure_scenario: The next hand reads 'rung 1' and 'unrepresentable', does the refactor, and records in the row that the labelling defect is now structurally impossible -- so no test is written for the construction site, and the swap lands there instead with the same 19 tests green. gate-design's ladder only helps if the rung is named honestly; a rung claimed one higher than it is buys a test being skipped.

findings.line: 265 (the M4.12 row, the 'What is covered' sentence)
findings.finding: THE COVERAGE SENTENCE OVER-CLAIMS TWICE AND ITS 'ABOVE' RESOLVES TO NOTHING. 'What is covered: the three fault classes on both conditional writes and on the three read verbs' -- but only ambiguousPut reaches putIfMatch (unreachable is drawn and deliberately not acted on at FaultInjectingStore.java:267, duplicatePut is drawn and discarded at :269), and only unreachable reaches stat/get/list. The row's own 'WHAT IS NOT MODELLED' paragraph states both facts three sentences later, so the row contradicts itself in one cell -- which is what keeps this cell mattering: it is the third consecutive round in which its coverage prose describes something other than the code. Separately, 'the five stream properties above' points at no list of five: the paragraph above it enumerates three failed attempts at per-class independence, and the five properties are enumerated in FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest's class javadoc, not in the row.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.15's milestone review reads backlog.md, which AGENTS.md calls authoritative, and takes 'the three fault classes on both conditional writes' at face value -- so M4.13's criterion 1 ('each injected fault class must have at least one seed where it changes the outcome') is believed to be met for duplicatePut on the lease CAS, when that class provably cannot reach it. The correcting paragraph is in the same cell but reads as a note about future work, not as a retraction of the sentence four lines up. Say 'ambiguousPut on both conditional writes, unreachable on putIfAbsent and on the three read verbs, duplicatePut on putIfAbsent' and the cell stops disagreeing with itself.

findings.line: 266 and 267 (the new M4.19 and M4.20 rows)
findings.finding: TWO VERBATIM DUPLICATED CLAUSES, both introduced by this revision's prose fixes. M4.19: 'Delivers I1-I5 as predicates over the raw objects, I1-I5 as predicates over the raw objects.' M4.20: '... with failover BOTH ways -- a polite release and a TTL lapse -- and fenced leaders that do not know it yet -- many logical pods, one seed, through the `Sequencer` seam, with failover both ways (a polite release and a TTL lapse) and fenced leaders that do not know it yet.' Both read as a splice left behind when the Y7/Y8 findings were addressed. AND M4.20 ASSERTS PRESENT-TENSE FACTS ABOUT FILES NOT IN THE TREE -- '`withZone` returns `this`, violating the `Clock` contract', 'the harness's own comment cites 6 commits and 3 takeovers' -- with none of the disclosure M4.19 got right in its first clause ('NEITHER IS TRACKED YET ... a fresh clone has none of it'). CommitProtocolSimulation.java and SimulatedClock.java are untracked and are not in this commit.
findings.failure_scenario: next-task picks up M4.20, greps for SimulatedClock in a fresh clone, finds nothing, and cannot tell whether the row describes a file that was deleted, one that was never committed, or one it is supposed to write -- the same ambiguity M4.19's disclosure was added to remove. The duplicated clauses are cheaper but land in the same place: a reader who has been trained by this backlog to read every clause as load-bearing spends the second reading looking for the distinction between the two copies. One sentence in M4.20 mirroring M4.19's 'NEITHER IS TRACKED YET', and two deletions, close both.
